content:
marta_cs: quick heads up — onboarding for CardioAI is stuck. They're getting a lot of preflight failures during SDK init from their edge warmup. Symptoms: lots of 401/429 in quick succession, tokens churned, and we see `x-rate-limit-remaining: 0` then `Retry-After` spikes. Can we triage fast?

dinesh_eng: is this the browser SDK in a serverless warmup (Cloudflare/Netlify edge) or a backend integration? logs please.

marta_cs: browser SDK inside a serverless warmup flow. snippet from their logs: 
```
[2026-03-22T17:02:12Z] POST /v1/preflight 401 "unauthenticated"
[2026-03-22T17:02:12Z] auth-refresh ok
[2026-03-22T17:02:13Z] POST /v1/preflight 429 x-rate-limit-remaining:0 retry-after: 30
[2026-03-22T17:02:13Z] token-request concurrent=18
```
They say they warm 50 instances in parallel during deploy.

kenji_dev: that `concurrent=18` lines and the TTL/refresh cadence smell like a token stampede. What does their SDK config look like?

marta_cs: they copied our quickstart — token TTL ~ 30s, heartbeat interval 5s, no jitter. here's the snippet they shared: 
```js
// client init in lambda warmup
const client = new RedwoodSDK({
  ephemeralTokenTTL: 30, // secs
  preflightHeartbeatMs: 5000,
  maxConcurrentPreflights: 0 // default
});
```

kenji_dev: yep — warmup x50 + TTL 30s + no jitter = synchronized refreshes. Quick wins: add jitter to heartbeat, set preflight throttle (maxConcurrentPreflights: 2), increase ephemeralTokenTTL (server-side policy can go to 120s for warmups), and prefetch tokens server-side. Example patch: 
```js
// add jitter + throttle
const jitter = () => Math.floor(Math.random() * 3000);
setTimeout(() => client.startPreflight(), 1000 + jitter());
client.configure({ maxConcurrentPreflights: 2 });
// ask ops to allow ephemeralTokenTTL=120 for this account while they warm
```

kenji_dev: also add exponential backoff for refresh failures, not tight spinning.

sana_support: tagging ops: we can do a temporary quota bump for CardioAI and enable a warmup allowance for 24h. To CS playbook: 1) advise jitter + throttle, 2) raise token TTL for warmup, 3) short-term quota bump, 4) confirm client uses Retry-After headers. I'll open a support ticket.

deploy-bot: Incident created: #CS-1209 "CardioAI preflight stampede" — assigned to infra oncall.

dinesh_eng: on infra/proxy side, coalescing preflights at the gateway helps too. If they're behind a proxy, set connection pool and limit parallel preflight requests per IP. Example nginx config: 
```
limit_conn_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=perip:10m;
limit_conn perip 2;
limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=reqip:10m rate=10r/s;
```
That plus honoring `Retry-After` mitigates the 429 flood.

sana_support: I added a small doc snippet for the customer with the minimal code changes and the short-term support steps (quota bump request sent). Link: https://redwood.example.com/docs/warmup-best-practices (internal).

marta_cs: plan for next 24h: 1) customer to patch SDK with jitter + maxConcurrentPreflights=2 (they said dev can ship this in ~30m) 2) support will apply ephemeralTokenTTL=120 + temporary quota bump, 3) infra to add per-ip rate limits if needed. Who will own the docs patch?

dinesh_eng: I can PR a tiny note in devex about warmup patterns and example nginx snippet.

marta_cs: perfect — I'll follow up with CardioAI and confirm once they redeploy. thanks all :thumbsup:
